newsitem.title: USA: Skater Baiul escapes drunk driving prosecution.
newsitem.headline: Skater Baiul escapes drunk driving prosecution.

text.p: A Connecticut judge on Tuesday permitted Olympic skating champion Oksana Baiul to enroll in an alcohol education programme, effectively granting her request to avoid prosecution on drunk driving charges.

Baiul, 19, was also fined the maximum $90 plus costs on a separate charge of driving too fast for conditions. The Ukrainian athlete pleaded no contest to the second charge and did not enter a plea on the first charge.
Under Connecticut law, the case will be expunged from her record when she completes the alcohol education programme.

Daniel Blume, her lawyer, told the court she would perform 25 hours of public service as part of the programme, but he said the details had yet to be worked out. "She's a fine person. She's going to benefit from this programme," Blume said.
The programme was designed "to educate rather than punish," he said. "She's fully aware of the gravity and seriousness of this matter."
Judge Terence Sullivan gave Baiul a stern lecture before handing down the sentence and reminded her she was two years below Connecticut's legal drinking age.
"You may be a celebrity, but you're not permitted to drink," he said. "You're just so incredibly fortunate, I don't think you realise it. You could have easily killed someone."

The judge, who said he had no power to suspend Baiul's license, urged her to throw herself into the community service. "If during the community service you can persuade one young person not to drink and drive ... you'll have done something very worthwhile. So I hope you'll put your whole heart and soul into the service."

Baiul, wearing a dark gray sweater suit, stood silently during the proceeding. She and her lawyers made no comment as they hustled through a crowd of reporters and photographers when leaving the courthouse.
Baiul, who lives in Simsbury, Connecticut, was originally charged with driving while intoxicated and reckless driving after she ran her Mercedes off a road and crashed on Jan. 12.
Prosecutor John O'Reilly told the court he lacked physical evidence to pursue the reckless driving charge so he substituted a charge of driving too fast for conditions.
Baiul had a blood-alcohol content of 0.168 percent at the time of the accident, according to a hospital report made public. The state's legal limit for adults is 0.10 percent.
